title: Target switching sensitivity starting range
summary: For target switching, a practical starting range is about 28-40 cm/360 because the task needs fast entries but still punishes unstable finishes and excess cleanup.
why: Target switching needs a balance between quick acquisition and controlled finish quality rather than pure flick speed.
A middle-to-faster range is usually easier for chaining fast entries together without making the finish unnecessarily messy.
actions: Start around 33 cm/360 and slow down slightly if the first snap is fast but your finish quality is messy.
If every switch feels heavy and you are late to the next target, test a modestly faster step.
Judge the setting by chaining and finish quality across multiple targets, not by one flashy snap.
avoid: Do not choose speed so aggressively that every switch needs extra cleanup.
Avoid overfitting the setup to one switching task if other switching widths feel completely wrong.
